text:
samir: Heads-up: ran a short ensemble canary of 'gull' fp16 + 'sparrow-lite' int8 + 'sparrow-lite-ptq' int4 for funcall structured outputs. The int4 variant sometimes drops the required "request_id" key in the funcall args, causing our strict schema validator to reject and trigger retries.

claire: how frequent? is this streaming-specific or seen on non-stream path too?

samir: non-stream path is fine. Streaming path with kv_prefix_trim and batch_size=2 shows drop from 0.05% -> 1.1% missing_key failures for the int4 replica. The ensemble routing then falls back and retries, which masks but increases latency and token cost.

ben: do you have an example raw reassembly? need to see whether the key is omitted or renamed/empty string.

samir: yep, captured one failure reassembled in order: 

samir: Assistant (stream): {
  "action": "create_ticket",
  "args": {
    "title": "Crash on save",
    "body": "app crashes when clicking save"
  }
}

samir: Notice missing "request_id" under args. In other successes we see: 

samir: Assistant (good): {
  "action": "create_ticket",
  "args": {
    "request_id": "r-9a3f",
    "title": "Crash on save",
    "body": "app crashes when clicking save"
  }
}

ops-bot: CI note: recent kernel-quant commit touched vocabulary remapping for escaped underscores (PR #2034). Flagging as potential covariate.

arun: theory: quantization altered tokenization so the short request_id pattern (alpha-numeric with dash) gets emitted as two tokens, and if a streaming chunk boundary aligns, our reassembler or parser/filter step may drop the first token (we've seen prefix-trim chop leading tokens). That would either make the key name malformed or remove the whole key.

lucy: can you repro deterministically? if it's repeatable we can diff token sequences across fp16/int8/int4 to pinpoint divergence.

samir: ran local repro with seed=2026, batch=2, kv_prefix_trim=true. Reproduced ~60% of attempts. I attached a tiny token offset dump in the logs (linked in ticket). Token-level diff shows int4 emits tokens: '"request', '_id"', ':' whereas fp16 emits '"request_id"', ':' as a single token. Reassembler treats '"request' as a partial key and sometimes discards it during prefix trim when chunks are small.

claire: interesting. So either we must avoid prefix-trim for short keys, or change sanitizer to reassemble at token-level and stitch split tokens before parse. Which is lower risk?

ben: token-level stitching is safer long-term but heavier. Short-term fix: if a key appears to be split across token boundaries (we can detect unmatched quote followed by underscore token), run a light stitch that glues adjacent token pieces at top-level before strict-parse. Record repaired=true. Also add a semantic-equality check (gold vs repaired) to avoid changing intent.

arun: agree. Also explore a quant-side fix: ensure vocab includes common identifier tokens like 'request_id' as atomic tokens for quantized builds (MODEL-620). Model team loop please.

ops-bot: created tickets MODEL-620 (quant vocab), RUNTIME-720 (token-stitch reassembler), EVAL-2112 (onboard test for split-key regressions). Links posted.

samir: prototype stitcher brought missing_key rate down to 0.12% on canary int4. Latency regressions due to retries dropped ~15% because fewer fallbacks.

lucy: we should add a metric in console: repaired_key_count and failed_strict_parses to monitor repairs vs real failures. If repaired grows over time it might hide model regressions.

claire: rollout plan: A) enable token-stitch reassembler on int4 streaming canary only, B) enable token-offset traces and repaired metrics, C) 48h run and require missing_key<=0.2% and false_repair_rate<0.05% before promoting to int8+fp16. D) if repairs stabilize, upstream model fix via MODEL-620.

ben: note: keep SDK parse helper opt-out so private customers with strict compliance can disable automatic stitching.

samir: I'll push the canary patch at 23:30 UTC and share a 12h snapshot. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

lucy: small test suggestion: include templates with short snake_case keys and numeric-ish ids to maximize chance of split and ensure our stitcher handles alphanum+underscore sequences robustly.

claire: thanks. end of thread.
